To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the damage to hair follicle structure and function is a function of the l.e.t.
the damage of a homogeneous population of hair cells by a heavy particle beam depends on the l.e.t. at the site of the beam entry into the tissue and the dose delivered.
the hair follicle is an excellent model to study the biological effects of ionizing radiation and that the response of hair follicles to heavy particle irradiaton is dose dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of the biological response of a biological structure to the increasing l.e. t. of a helium beam, which is of interest for the evaluation of heavy particle radiation therapy and space radiation protection.
a detailed investigation of the biological effect of heavy particle irradiation in a well defined biological system.
the development and use of a new method for studying the response of a biological target to the l.e.t. range of a helium ion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1. hair follicles in different sites on the rat tail respond differently to the same helium dose, 2. the damage increases with the l.e.t., 3. the damage increases linearly with the dose.
the damage induced in a biological system by heavy particle irradiation is not a function of the l.e.t., but rather a function of the dose.
the hair follicle is a sensitive biological system to be used in the study of heavy ion radiation effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dose of 10 Gy at 0.8 MeV/nucleon (l.e.t. 0.8 mm) is enough to cause a complete hair follicle destruction.
the damage induced by the helium ion beam is a function of the l.e.t. and the dose.
the damage induced in hair follicles after irradiation with a heavy particle beam is not a function of the dose delivered but of the l.e.t.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the damage to hair follicles is a function of the l.e.t.
the hair follicles of the rat tail represent an interesting model for the analysis of the in vivo effects of heavy particle radiation.
the damage to the hair follicle is a function of the l.e.t. at the site of irradiation.
